about: The Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed, said after the Gospel on every Sunday and on the greater feasts, and left out in Masses for the Dead. All genuflect at Et incarnátus est, where the Creed confesses the Word made flesh. Its articles run from the Father and the Son to the Holy Spirit, the Church, one baptism, the resurrection of the dead and the life of the world to come.

seg.nr: At the middle of the altar, the priest extends and raises his hands, joins them, says the Creed if prescribed, and continues with hands joined. The priest bows his head to the cross at in unum Deum, at Iesum Christum and at simul adorátur, and signs himself from forehead to breast at Et vitam ventúri sǽculi.

seg.tr: I believe in one God, the almighty Father, maker of heaven and earth, of all things visible and invisible.
And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God.
And born of the Father before all ages.
God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God.
Begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father; through whom all things were made.

fn.w050: With “sunt” (w051), forms the perfect passive “facta sunt”: “were made”.

seg.tr: Who, for us human beings and for our salvation, came down from heaven.

seg.nr: Here a genuflection is made, held from Et incarnátus est through et homo factus est, and then all rise.

seg.tr: And He was incarnate by the Holy Spirit from the Virgin Mary, and became man.

fn.w064: With “est” (w065), forms the perfect “incarnátus est”: “was made flesh”.
fn.w074: With “est” (w075), forms the perfect “factus est”. “homo” (w073) is the predicate nominative.

seg.tr: He was also crucified for us; He suffered under Pontius Pilate and was buried.

fn.w083: Participle of a deponent verb — passive form, active meaning: the one who suffered.

seg.tr: And He rose again on the third day, according to the Scriptures.

fn.w090: Ablative of time. Feminine here, agreeing with “tértia” (w089).

seg.tr: And He ascended into heaven and sits at the Father's right hand.
And He will come again in glory to judge the living and the dead; His kingdom will have no end.

fn.w107: The infinitive states the purpose of His coming: “He will come to judge the living and the dead”.
fn.w111: Possessive genitive modifying “regni” (w112), with Christ as its antecedent.

seg.tr: And I believe in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and giver of life, who proceeds from the Father and the Son.

fn.w122: A present participle serving as a title: literally “the one giving life”.
fn.w126: The enclitic conjunction “-que” means “and”: “ex Patre Filióque”, “from the Father and the Son”.

seg.tr: Who is adored and glorified together with the Father and the Son; who spoke through the prophets.

fn.w138: A deponent participle with “est” (w139): locútus est — “spoke”. Passive form, active meaning.

seg.tr: And I believe in one holy, catholic and apostolic Church.
I confess one baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
And I await the resurrection of the dead.
And the life of the world to come. Amen.

fn.w161: The future participle in the genitive, agreeing with “sǽculi” (w162): literally “of the age that is to come”.
